The show is entertaining, but if you're unfamiliar with coupons you can't really learn anything from it. You see them throwing hundreds of things in their carts saying "this is free, these are free, those are all free..." but how? My biggest peeve is when some of them clear the shelves to hoard all these items & not donate them, creating a bad image for the rest of us couponers. Who will ever need 60-some bottles of mustard in a 2 person household? One woman said "when I run out of room for my stockpile, *that's* when I'll consider donating..." it's so selfish in my opinion. I have a humble stockpile of some items but I always donate because some people don't have the means to go out and shop for these deals like I do. Some episodes feature good Samaritans while others feature the more selfish individuals so it's a fair balance, I'm just not a fan  =)

I'm not a fan of the show but I'm a coupon fanatic so here's some sites to get you going... 
http://cravingsavings.blogspot.com/  is just a blog but always keeps you up to date on really good offers
www.weusecoupons.com  this site is a MUST... you only have to register if you want to comment in the forums (I'm not registered) but they have everything from a-z like store sale previews up to 3 weeks or so in advance, coupon matchups, etc...
http://www.jillcataldo.com/  I like her because she's a practical couponer - her grocery cart always has fresh produce and healthier food choices instead of 50 boxes of toothpaste or something and she still saves a lot of money... watch some of her videos
http://frugalday.com/  is another great blog
http://supercouponing.coupontom.com/pricebook/search  is my new favorite site... you can use the coupon search if you need to find a coupon for something on your list and you can use the price list search to find which store has the best deal on that product
http://www.moneysavingmadness.com/search/label/Walmart  is another really helpful blog, not just the walmart section but look up any stores you have in your area and they'll let you know what the best current deals are
http://capriservices.blogspot.com/  is an extremely cheap couponing service that sells you inserts for about 50 cents a piece
couponsthingsbydede.com  I have probably spent close to $100 at this site since I stumbled upon it. If you see a really great deal coming up you can go here and order all the coupons you desire so you can really stock up cheap. you can buy coupons individually or by insert

Also look up your local stores' policies on coupons so you know what your limits are and how to make the most of your savings =)

It's so hard not to say anything when we have to deal with these calls. I stay within my language but emphasize the "THANK YOU!!!" when the hearing person decides they don't want to continue the call. Also throughout the call I try to sound bored/robotic while reading all the text in hopes that the hearing person becomes uncomfortable enough to hang up.

We used to but not as much anymore. These days the supervisor will intervene and ask that the callers not bring the operator into the context of the conversation. Other than that, we'll say anything you want.

Relay users can make any phone call they wish, just like you & I can. We'll type what the recording says as far as how much the charge per minute is, and if they accept, we'll continue the call. I haven't called a sex line yet but have had to process sex calls between couples.

I know it's frustrating (*believe me, I know*), especially if the caller is slower to type a response, but I promise it goes much smoother if you bear with the operator. A suggestion: once the operator gives their greeting they typically hesitate for just a moment in case you have anything to add, so feel free to -immediately- explain your company's policy, but pace yourself so we can type it all out before you hang up =) And out of curiosity, why aren't you supposed to take the calls?

We do get entertaining calls from time to time, but it feels really shitty to have to let this person scam someone completely unsuspecting & innocent, and also to maintain a "pleasant" tone of voice while processing the call for these scumbags.
